editorial:
Imagine trying to run away from your own sadness by working twenty hours a day during the holidays. That is exactly what you get with this story. You follow a woman who is totally heartbroken after losing her mom, but instead of crying, she buries herself in spreadsheets and emails. It starts off feeling very stressful, but it quickly turns into a funny and touching look at how people deal with grief. The vibe is bright and colorful, which makes the sad parts feel a bit more hopeful. You will feel for her as she tries to keep it all together while the world around her is celebrating.

What really makes this work is the lead actress, who makes you feel every bit of her stress until that big panic attack changes everything. The pacing is steady, though some might find the middle a bit slow. If you enjoy stories about family and finding yourself, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the main character finally stops running and has a heart-to-heart with her sister. She realizes that working herself to death was just a way to avoid saying goodbye to her mother. The twist is that she finds a hidden letter from her mom telling her to slow down and enjoy life. She quits her stressful job and spends the rest of the holiday relaxing, finally finding peace with her loss.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and stories about healing.
